text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Land Transport Authority looking at ways to ease worsening traffic congestion on main expressways, including Pan Island Expressway and Central Expressway.

- Lawyer Tang Liang Hong's statement last week that People's Action Party leaders were out to ruin him politically and financially with their lawsuits was "a very serious allegation", Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong says.
- A child's tricycle thrown from a high kitchen window landed on a new Proton Wira on Saturday, damaging the car badly.
- Singaporean property investors remain number one Asian buyers of homes on Australia's popular Gold Coast in 1996.
- Initial public offer (IPO) fever drives retail investors to punp Singapore $1.83 billion into applications for only S$82.5 million worth of shares available in this year's first five IPOs.
- Japanese government tells country's three international telecommunications companies they can block customers from connecting to overseas discount "callback" services.
- Earnings growth for Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is likely to slow in second half of financial year after impressive 39 percent jump in group net profit in first half, analysts say.
- Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index could gain about 200 points this year from present level due to Malaysia's attractive interest rates, forecaster David Fuller says.
- Leading Asian stock markets buoyed by wave of Japanese institutional investment fleeing miserable returns available in Japan's own financial markets.
- Realistic pricing could eventually break homebuyers' resistance to 99-year leasehold landed property, property consultants say.
- PT Trans-Pacific Petrochemical Indotama, one of Indonesia's fastest growing business groups, enters into joint venture to build US$2.3 billion petrochemicals complex in East Java.
- Singapore stock market ripe for rebound on back of foreign investment flows amid economic recovery led by pickup in manufacturing sector, leading investment houses predict.
- Lowering of Malaysia's November 1996 trade deficit to 523 million ringgit should give market a leg-up this week.
- Precision engineering group Cam International Holdings calls off major deal to make disk drives for two foreign companies following unresolved disputes.
